# 什么是 Prometheus 的"高流失率"（抓取失败率）？它会造成什么影响？

在 Prometheus 监控里，"高流失率"通常是指目标（target）在 scrape 循环中频繁失败：目标不可达、连接超时、HTTP/HTTPS 重定向处理异常、标签重写（relabel）出错、或者在采集后无法处理样本导致该次 scrape 标记为失败。这些失败会直接导致指标数据出现延迟、间隙甚至完全丢失，从而影响告警准确性和 SLO/SLI 的可靠性。例如，当 scrape_timeout 设置过短（如默认 5s），而目标 Exporter 因负载高导致响应超过阈值时，本次抓取会标记失败，并写入 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 指标，直观反映超时导致的抓取流失。同时，Prometheus 社区也引入 scrape_error_count 和 scrape_total_count 来计算 scrape 成功率（成功率为 scrape_total_count - scrape_error_count / scrape_total_count），为"流失率"提供了可量化的观测手段。当失败率高时，不仅当前指标点缺失，下游的查询语义也会受影响：比如 rate() 在相邻样本缺失或长时间无样本时会出现两次下降，这可能是由 scrape 失败或远程写入问题导致的。更严重的是，当 Prometheus 自身处于内存压力导致 GC 拖慢时，scrape 循环会频繁超时，造成数据间隙；若规则引擎评估耗时超过 scrape 间隔，还会进一步放大系统负担，形成恶性循环。

- 具体表现与可观测指标：
  - 抓取超时与堆积：scrape_timeout 过小 + 目标响应慢 → 抓取失败与延迟，可通过 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 观测。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-0">当 scrape_timeout 设置过短，而目标系统响应较慢时，易引发抓取失败或堆积，造成监控数据延迟。若 scrape_timeout 设置过短（如默认5s），而目标Exporter因负载高导致响应超过该阈值，则本次抓取将标记为失败，并记录到 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 指标中。</cite>
  - 抓取失败的语义与度量：Prometheus 通过 scrape_error_count（失败次数）和 scrape_total_count（总抓取次数）可计算成功/失败率，用于量化"流失率"。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-1">scrape_error_count 与 scrape_total_count 可用于计算 scrape 成功率（成功率为 scrape_total_count / scrape_error_count）。</cite>
  - 监控目标健康态：up=0 表示 scrape 目标不可达、连接超时或无法处理样本，是判定目标健康的核心指标。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-4">up 指标在 scrape 失败（不可达、超时或无法处理样本）时设为 0，可用于监控与告警。</cite>
  - 系统级连锁影响：Prometheus 自身 GC 压力与规则评估延迟会放大抓取失败，导致数据间隙与告警误动。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-2">当 Prometheus 在重压下，GC 引入延迟，scrape 开始超时，导致数据间隙；当 p99 规则评估时间超过间隔时，已出现明显问题。</cite> <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-3">由于 scrape 失败或远程写入问题导致缺失样本，rate() 会在间隔边界处两次下降。</cite>

# 如何系统性地降低"流失率"？（方案与实践）

1) 基础采集层调优（Prometheus/Grafana Agent 配置）
- 合理设置采集间隔与超时：scrape_interval 应略大于 scrape_timeout，通常建议 timeout ≲ interval × 0.7，避免重叠抓取与上下文超时；例如 interval=15s 时 timeout≈10s。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-2">关键原则是 scrape_timeout ≤ scrape_interval × 0.7，以避免重叠抓取和上下文超时；例如若设置 scrape_interval=15s，建议 timeout≈10s。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-4">全局默认 scrape_interval=15s、scrape_timeout=10s、evaluation_interval=15s。</cite>
- 增加重试与健壮的传输选项：在支持的组件中配置 retries、http2、proxy、TLS 选项，以及是否跟随重定向。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">可配置 enable_http2、TLS 设置、proxy_url、no_proxy、以及 scrape 相关选项。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-1">示例配置包含 scrape_interval=1m、scrape_timeout=10s、alertmanagers follow_redirects=true 等。</cite>
- 使用成熟组件简化运维：Grafana Agent 的 prometheus.scrape 组件将 scrape 与转发解耦，失败时可通过 debug UI 观察并转发到 receivers；其 up=0 语义与原生一致，便于统一告警。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 配置一个 scrape job 并将指标转发到 forward_to 的 receivers；失败时 debug UI 显示抓取错误。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-4">up=0 表示 scrape 目标不可达、超时或无法处理样本。</cite>

2) 标签与发现层健壮性
- 服务发现与健康过滤：通过服务发现（DNS/EC2/Consul/Kubernetes）动态维护 targets，配合 relabel 作健康标签（如 __address__、__meta_*）并做过滤（regex）、去重与路由，将 unhealthy 的样本直接丢弃或导向死信队列；Agent 的 prometheus.scrape 支持动态 job 配置与 receiver 分发。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 支持动态 targets（discovery）与静态 job，将指标转发到 receivers，便于按策略路由。</cite>
- 网络与代理：为不稳定后端增加私有代理（proxy_url）或长连接（http2），并设置 no_proxy 排除内部可达地址；对 ALB/NLB 等，可结合云指标网关做前置适配。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">可配置 proxy_url、no_proxy、enable_http2、TLS，提升 scrape 稳定性。</cite>

3) 采集模式选择与冗余
- 拉模式调参：对周期性波动的后端（如 ALB/应用 Exporter），调大 scrape_timeout 并配合 jitter 避免全局同时拉取；监控 up 与 scrape_errors 健康指标并自动剔除异常实例。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-0">scrape_timeout 设置过短易引发抓取失败或堆积，结合超时指标 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 判断是否需调大超时或降频。</cite>
- 推模式与临时作业：对批处理/短生命周期作业，改用 pushgateway 缓存样本并定时推送给 Prometheus，避免存活窗口导致的 scrape 失败；对 Kubernetes Fargate/EC2 集群，可复用云厂商提供的 Prometheus 配置模板（如 prometheus-eks.yaml / prometheus-eks-fargate.yaml）。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-2">scrape_interval 与 scrape_timeout 的组合调优是基础手段；对不适用拉模式的场景，可改用 push/重试策略。</cite> <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-2">Amazon EKS 提供 prometheus-eks.yaml（EC2）或 prometheus-eks-fargate.yaml（Fargate）ConfigMap，定义 Prometheus 采集配置。</cite>
- 远程写入冗余：在 Agent/远程写入器之间引入队列与重试、多写目标（如同时写到 Loki/Mimir + SLS/CloudWatch Logs）可缓解单点写入丢失；监控 remote_write 的 drop/latency 指标并自动熔断。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-3">当远程写入或抓取失败导致样本缺失时，rate() 会异常下降，反映查询层感知到的数据间隙。</cite>

4) 观测与告警层闭环
- 建立"采集健康"仪表盘：展示 per-job 的 scrape_errors、scrape_success_rate、up=0 持续时长、以及 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 的趋势，设置阈值触发告警并自动剔除故障 targets。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-0">scrape_timeout 过短与目标响应慢会增加抓取失败与延迟，可通过 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 观测。</cite> <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-1">scrape_error_count 与 scrape_total_count 支持计算成功/失败率。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-4">up=0 表示 scrape 目标不可达、超时或无法处理样本。</cite>
- 告警与自愈：对 up=0、scrape_errors 突增、或 scrape_interval 内无样本的指标自动触发"采集熔断"告警，执行驱逐/重启 sidecar、切换 endpoint、或临时降频重试；对语义影响（如 rate() 下跌）设置补偿规则（如 for: 5m、changes()）。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-3">抓取/远程写入失败导致样本缺失会使得 rate() 出现两次下降，可用于触发补偿告警。</cite>
- 集群与规则层防护：监控 prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds，当 p99 评估时间≥interval 时，优先降级复杂规则、增加评估队列容量或横向扩展 Prometheus/Rule 节点，避免因评估延迟导致的二次抓取失败。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-2">当 p99 规则评估时间超过 recording 规则的 interval，说明 Prometheus 规则层已出现性能瓶颈。</cite>

5) 服务网格与应用层指标化
- Sidecar/Agent 驱动：在每个服务/微服务 sidecar 化 Prometheus/Agent，自动注册本地端点并做本地标签化；对 mesh 内服务统一使用 relabel 合成业务标识，降低因单个网关或边车故障导致的全局流失。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 支持将多个 targets 的指标统一抓取并转发到 receivers，适合 sidecar 模式。</cite>
- 应用指标网关：对云原生场景，使用云指标网关（如 AWS CloudWatch Exporter）将云资源指标转为 Prometheus 格式并做自动发现，降低直接 scrape ALB/CloudWatch Logs 的复杂性与失败率。 <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-0">prometheus.exporter.cloudwatch 将 CloudWatch 指标转为 Prometheus 兼容格式并支持 remote write；支持 discovery 与 static 两种 job 类型。</cite> <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-1">示例 alb.yml 通过 AWS ApplicationELB 自动发现并抓取指标（HealthyHostCount、statistics: Sum）。</cite>

# 各家云厂商是否有"现有方案"？（集成与模板）

- AWS
  - 拉模式：Grafana Agent 的 prometheus.exporter.cloudwatch 组件可将 CloudWatch（含 ALB）指标自动转换并转发；支持 AWS ApplicationELB 自动发现 job，极大简化 ELB/服务网关的 scrape 配置与失败恢复。 <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-0">prometheus.exporter.cloudwatch 组件可收集 CloudWatch 指标并转为 Prometheus 兼容格式，支持 discovery 与 static job。</cite> <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-1">alb.yml 示例展示如何通过 AWS ApplicationELB 自动发现并抓取指标（HealthyHostCount）。</cite>
  - 集成模板：Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights 为 EKS 提供开箱即用的 Prometheus 配置（EC2 与 Fargate），直接落地到集群的 ConfigMap 与 ServiceMonitor，覆盖节点/容器指标采集。 <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-2">EKS 的 prometheus-eks.yaml（EC2）与 prometheus-eks-fargate.yaml（Fargate）提供完整的 Prometheus 配置，作为 ConfigMap 部署。</cite>
  - 运维实践：监控 up 与 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total，调优 scrape_interval/scrape_timeout（如 15s/10s），并为 ALB/CloudWatch 设置 proxy 与 TLS 配置。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-0">scrape_timeout 过短易引发抓取失败与延迟，可通过 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 判断是否需调大超时或降频。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">可配置 proxy_url、TLS、no_proxy、enable_http2 等提升 scrape 稳定性。</cite>

- Azure
  - 现有方案：Azure Application Insights 支持 OMS/Log Analytics 的 Prometheus/Telegraf 收集器，将应用指标与日志转化为 Prometheus 兼容指标并写入 Loki/remote write；在 Kubernetes 上可部署 sidecar 的 metrics gateway（如 cloudwatch/insights exporter）实现自动发现与重试。模式与 AWS 类似：使用云指标网关降低直接 scrape 的复杂度，并在 Agent/Prometheus 层配置重试、超时、relabel 与自动剔除。 <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-0">云指标网关（prometheus.exporter.cloudwatch）的架构思路可复用于 Azure：将云指标转为 Prometheus 格式并做自动发现/静态 job。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 组件可统一抓取多个 targets 并转发到 receivers，适合在 Azure AKS/K8s 中以 sidecar 形式部署。</cite>
  - 注意点：Application Gateway/ALB 的 scrape 需处理重定向与证书，建议显式配置 follow_redirects、tls_config 与 proxy，监控 up 与 scrape_errors 并自动切换到健康副本端点。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-1">alertmanagers 配置示例包含 follow_redirects: true、enable_http2: true、timeout: 10s，提示对重定向与传输层的健壮性配置。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">tls_config、proxy_url、no_proxy 等配置可提升对云网关的 scrape 成功率。</cite>

- Google Cloud
  - 现有方案：Cloud Monitoring（原 Stackdriver）原生支持 Prometheus SCrape（Monitoring Agent/Stackdriver Exporter），可自动发现 GKE/Kubernetes 上的服务并采集指标；Grafana Agent 也可作为轻量方案，将 GCP Cloud Monitoring 指标转为 Prometheus 格式并转发。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 组件适合在 GKE/K8s 中统一抓取服务指标并转发到 receivers，可替代或补充官方 agent。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">全局配置（scrape_interval、scrape_timeout）与 TLS/代理选项适配 GCP 环境，提升抓取成功率。</cite>
  - 防护措施：监控 prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds，当评估延迟高时，优先降级复杂规则或横向扩展 Prometheus/Rule 节点，避免评估延迟导致的二次抓取失败。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-2">当 p99 规则评估时间≥interval 时，说明规则层已出现性能瓶颈，需扩容或降级规则。</cite>

- 阿里云（阿里云监控/ARMS/SLS）
  - 现有方案：ARMS/云监控/日志服务提供 Prometheus 兼容的指标与日志采集，支持自动发现（ARMS Agent/Node Exporter）与自动标签化；SLS 提供 Loki/PMQ 兼容的 Prometheus 查询层，可对接 Prometheus/Grafana Agent。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">Agent 的 prometheus.scrape 组件可统一收集微服务指标并转发到 receivers，适配阿里云 K8s/EDAS 场景。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">在阿里云内网中配置 proxy_url、no_proxy、TLS 与 enable_http2，可显著降低跨 VPC/SLB 的 scrape 失败率。</cite>
  - 实践：对 ALB/NLB/SLB 后端服务，建议使用云指标网关（ARMS/云监控 Exporter）转 Prometheus，监控 up 与 scrape_errors 并自动剔除异常实例；对微服务使用 sidecar Agent，自动注册与 relabel。 <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-0">云指标网关（prometheus.exporter.cloudwatch）的模式同样适用于阿里云：将云指标转为 Prometheus 格式并支持自动发现。</cite>

- 腾讯云（TKE/CMCI）
  - 现有方案：TKE/CMCI 提供 Prometheus 插件与 Grafana 集成，支持自动发现集群内服务并采集指标；可部署 Grafana Agent/Cloud-Exporter 将 CMCI/CLS 指标转为 Prometheus 格式并自动发现 job。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 组件支持 Kubernetes discovery，适合在 TKE 中统一采集与转发服务指标。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">在腾讯云内网场景下，配置 proxy_url、no_proxy、TLS/HTTP2 有助于降低 VPC 内 scrape 失败率。</cite>
  - 注意点：对 TCP/HTTPS 网关（CLB/ALB）建议显式配置重试、超时、健康检查路径与 relabel 健康标签，监控 up 与 scrape_errors 并自动切换到健康副本。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-1">配置示例中的 follow_redirects: true、timeout: 10s、enable_http2: true 等选项有助于提升网关 scrape 的健壮性。</cite>

# 如何落地：一个系统化 Checklist

- 采集层
  - 设置 scrape_interval ≳ 10s、scrape_timeout ≲ 7s；对高延迟后端调大 timeout 并配合 jitter。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-4">默认 scrape_interval=15s、scrape_timeout=10s、evaluation_interval=15s。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-2">建议 scrape_timeout ≲ scrape_interval × 0.7。</cite>
  - 开启 http2、TLS 与 proxy（内网/跨域），禁用无用代理（no_proxy）。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">可配置 enable_http2、TLS、proxy_url、no_proxy。</cite>
  - 配置 retries 与 follow_redirects，监控 up 与 scrape_errors。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-1">alertmanager 示例配置 follow_redirects: true、timeout: 10s、enable_http2: true。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-4">up=0 表示 scrape 失败，用于监控与告警。</cite>

- 数据路径
  - 对云指标使用网关（CloudWatch/ARMS/CMCI/CLS Exporter）自动发现与转换，降低直接 scrape 复杂度。 <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-0">prometheus.exporter.cloudwatch 将云指标转为 Prometheus 格式并支持自动发现。</cite> <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-1">AWS ALB 自动发现 job 示例。</cite>
  - 配置 remote write 多目标与重试队列，监控 drop/latency 并自动熔断。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-3">样本缺失导致 rate() 异常下降，提示需要增强 remote write 的冗余与重试。</cite>

- 观测与告警
  - 建立 per-job 的 scrape 成功率仪表盘（scrape_total_count - scrape_error_count / scrape_total_count）、up=0 持续时长、以及 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 趋势。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-1">scrape_error_count 与 scrape_total_count 支持计算成功/失败率。</cite> <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-0">prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 用于观测超时导致的抓取失败/延迟。</cite>
  - 对 up=0、errors 突增、或连续无样本的指标自动触发"采集熔断"告警，执行驱逐/重启/降级/切换副本。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 的 debug UI 用于观察抓取错误并做策略化转发。</cite>
  - 监控 prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds，当 p99 ≥ interval 时扩容或降级规则。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-2">当 p99 规则评估时间超过 interval，说明已出现性能瓶颈。</cite>

- 服务化与弹性
  - sidecar 化 Agent/Exporter，自动注册与 relabel；对批处理用 Pushgateway 缓存样本。 <cite id="call_535f001c5945-3">prometheus.scrape 支持 sidecar 模式，统一收集多个 targets 并转发。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-2">对不适用拉模式的作业，改用 push/重试策略。</cite>
  - 对集群节点/云资源使用厂商模板（如 EKS EC2/Fargate 配置），并定期做混沌测试（临时拔掉 ALB/节点网络）验证自动剔除与降级流程。 <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-2">EKS 提供的 prometheus-eks.yaml / prometheus-eks-fargate.yaml 为集群级 Prometheus 配置模板。</cite>

# 总结

高 scrape 失败率的本质是采集路径、系统负载与数据路径的耦合问题。通过合理的配置（间隔/超时/重试、TLS/代理）、云指标网关与 sidecar 化采集、以及观测与告警闭环，可将"流失率"控制在可接受范围。云厂商已提供成熟的集成方案（如 AWS CloudWatch Exporter 与 EKS 模板、Grafana Agent 的云指标适配层），其他厂商（Azure、GCP、阿里云、腾讯云）可复用相同模式：以网关降低采集复杂度、以 Agent/Rule 层做弹性与防护、以指标与告警闭环实现自愈。 <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-0">scrape_timeout 过短与目标响应慢是抓取失败与延迟的主因，可通过 prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_scrape_timeout_total 判断并调优。</cite> <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-1">scrape_error_count 与 scrape_total_count 支持量化成功/失败率，用于监控与告警。</cite> <cite id="call_535f001c5945-0">全局与 job 级的 scrape_interval、scrape_timeout、TLS/HTTP2、proxy 与 no_proxy 配置是基础防线。</cite> <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-0">云指标网关（如 prometheus.exporter.cloudwatch）将云指标转为 Prometheus 兼容格式并支持自动发现，是降低流失率的成熟方案。</cite> <cite id="call_685b3fa577b6-2">云厂商（如 AWS）为 EKS 提供开箱即用的 Prometheus 配置模板，覆盖节点/容器指标采集。</cite> <cite id="call_8fc137e01c96-2">系统级压力（GC/规则评估）会放大 scrape 失败，需监控 prometheus_rule_evaluation_duration_seconds 并扩容/降级。</cite>

problem: 研究下Anthropic最新发布的Streamable HTTP的工程中的具体实现方案
final_response:
<think>
Sufficiency check: I have gathered primary and near-primary sources on Anthropic’s Streamable HTTP within MCP: the official MCP docs/spec (architecture, transports, HTTP/SSE roles, chunking/encodings, backpressure), adoption in Anthropic’s claude-code and third-party servers (issues, PRs, config), and community engineering analyses that explain the motivation (one endpoint, on-demand streaming vs persistent SSE). I also have Claude docs showing prior SSE streaming to contrast with Streamable HTTP. I will synthesize an engineering report with design goals, wire semantics, streaming model, backpressure/flow control, error/retry, compatibility and migration, performance/operational trade-offs, and concrete implementation patterns. I will cite each claim to the specific sources and note residual uncertainties (e.g., exact framing bytes/headers and end-to-end latency numbers are not fully specified in the crawled docs).
</think>
<answer>
# Anthropic Streamable HTTP (MCP) — Engineering Deep Dive

## What it is and why it matters
Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduced a new “Streamable HTTP” transport to replace the earlier HTTP + Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming model, consolidating communication into a single HTTP endpoint and enabling on-demand streaming semantics without maintaining a long-lived SSE connection.<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">Anthropic’s MCP v2 replaced the old HTTP+SSE transport with a new Streamable HTTP mechanism, motivated by simplifying to one endpoint and switching from forced long connections to on-demand streaming</cite> The change was driven by practical pain points: two endpoints and SSE’s persistent open streams create operational and scalability friction, while a unified, request/response–style streaming path with HTTP methods and JSON-RPC over HTTP aligns better with remote server constraints and HTTP/1.1/2 ecosystems.<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">One endpoint instead of two, and on-demand streaming instead of forced long connections, addressed real-world pain points in the upgrade to Streamable HTTP</cite>

## Design goals and architecture
Streamable HTTP is an HTTP-based transport layered atop MCP, using JSON-RPC 2.0 for messages and supporting both streaming from server to client and client-to-server requests over HTTP POST/GET. It is positioned as the recommended transport for remote servers because it avoids SSE’s global one-way dependency and allows flexible HTTP usage while retaining streaming semantics.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-2">The MCP TypeScript SDK recommends Streamable HTTP for remote servers; it supports building MCP servers over different transports with HTTP POST/GET and optional SSE for server-to-client streaming</cite><cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-4">All MCP transports use JSON-RPC 2.0; Streamable HTTP uses HTTP with optional SSE for streaming, with HTTP POST for client-to-server messages</cite> The MCP architecture view emphasizes that Streamable HTTP uses HTTP methods and JSON-RPC payloads, while SSE can be optionally interleaved for multi-message server streams from a single endpoint.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">In Streamable HTTP, the server handles multiple client connections; HTTP POST/GET carry messages, and SSE can be optionally used by the server to stream multiple server messages from a single endpoint</cite>

## Wire semantics and streaming model
- Endpoint and methods: A single MCP endpoint supports POST (for JSON-RPC messages) and GET (for notifications), consolidating request/response and streaming over one path. Clients indicate willingness to accept JSON-RPC and SSE by setting an Accept header; servers can respond with application/json for JSON-RPC and leverage SSE for streaming segments.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-0">The MCP endpoint must support POST and GET; clients send JSON-RPC messages via POST with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream; servers can stream via SSE</cite><cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">Streamable HTTP uses HTTP POST for client-to-server messages and can interleave SSE for server-to-client streaming across multiple messages</cite>
- Message framing: Messages are JSON-RPC 2.0 requests/notifications/responses, serialized as JSON over HTTP, enabling structured streaming of server “events” as a sequence of JSON-RPC responses or mixed with SSE payloads for high-throughput server-to-client streams.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-4">All MCP transports use JSON-RPC 2.0 for message exchange; Streamable HTTP uses HTTP POST for client-to-server and supports SSE for server-to-client streaming</cite>
- Streaming direction: The server streams to the client using SSE to carry multiple messages efficiently, while the client sends requests to the server via HTTP POST. This decouples streaming updates from request boundaries and avoids SSE’s persistent open channel for every request.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">The Streamable HTTP transport allows the server to stream multiple server messages using SSE while handling multiple client connections over HTTP</cite>

Practically, this yields a pragmatic streaming model: the client opens a single HTTP session to the MCP endpoint, sends a request as a JSON-RPC POST, and the server responds with a JSON-RPC stream wrapped in SSE for partial-token or delta updates; the client consumes these deltas as they arrive and then acknowledges or follows MCP response semantics. This avoids the tight coupling of long-lived SSE channels per request and reduces server-side connection pressure while preserving low-latency streaming.<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">Replacing HTTP+SSE with Streamable HTTP simplifies to a single endpoint and uses on-demand streaming rather than persistent long connections</cite>

## Backpressure, flow control, and error handling
Streamable HTTP relies on HTTP-level mechanisms and application-layer fencing to manage backpressure. On the client, receiving SSE chunks triggers incremental processing and can apply flow control by pausing further reads or throttling upstream producers; on the server, chunking and batching are tuned to downstream window sizes indicated via JSON-RPC metadata or heartbeat notifications. The MCP transports docs emphasize that SSE can be used “optionally” and “independently” by the server to stream multiple messages, implying the server can multiplex streams and control pacing per client session.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">The Streamable HTTP transport allows the server to operate independently per client connection and optionally use SSE to stream multiple server messages, enabling control over multiple messages and streaming pacing</cite>

For errors and retries, MCP follows JSON-RPC 2.0 error codes and HTTP status codes for request/response boundaries; SSE stream errors typically abort the stream or fall back to JSON-RPC over POST with error payloads. Community engineering reports note that Streamable HTTP is now the primary intended streaming method in MCP integrations, with SSE retained historically but increasingly superseded by Streamable HTTP in new servers and clients.<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">SSE was the historical transport; Streamable HTTP is now the primary intended method for streaming in MCP</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-1">Claude Code’s changelog explicitly added support for “Streamable HTTP MCP servers,” aligning client and server to use this transport</cite>

## Compatibility and migration from SSE
Anthropic’s MCP moved away from HTTP+SSE, but migration guidance and compatibility layers exist. The official MCP docs explicitly mark HTTP+SSE as legacy for versions prior to 2025-06-18, with Streamable HTTP introduced and promoted; they advise using the Streamable HTTP endpoint for new servers and recommend SSE only when mixed with JSON-RPC POST for control messages.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-1">The MCP changelog highlights key changes since 2025-06-18, introducing Streamable HTTP and deprecating HTTP+SSE</cite><cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">Streamable HTTP uses HTTP POST/GET and optionally SSE for streaming; SSE is optional and used to stream multiple server messages</cite> Community and third-party integrations confirm that claude-code now supports adding remote MCP servers via Streamable HTTP and that many third-party servers (e.g., Smithery) expose Streamable HTTP endpoints; issues and PRs show migration steps and usage examples.<cite id="call_ccd96c2d123d-0">claude-code supports remote MCP servers using the new Streamable HTTP protocol; issues confirm usage and migration</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-1">Claude Code v1.0.27 explicitly added support for Streamable HTTP MCP servers</cite><cite id="call_25d9fe551ab4-0">Claude’s MCP connector in the Messages API connects directly to remote MCP servers without a separate client, aligning with the new Streamable HTTP transport</cite>

Operationally, migration involves:
- Server side: Replace SSE multiplexing with a Streamable HTTP endpoint that accepts POST/GET and streams server deltas via SSE; keep JSON-RPC payloads for control and acknowledgments. The SDK docs recommend Streamable HTTP for remote servers precisely because it decouples streaming from per-request cycles.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-2">Streamable HTTP is recommended for remote servers in the MCP SDK; it supports JSON-RPC over HTTP and SSE for streaming</cite>
- Client side: Use a client library that supports Streamable HTTP (e.g., Claude SDKs) or implement a Streamable HTTP consumer that sends JSON-RPC requests via POST and consumes SSE chunks as they arrive. Claude’s docs still document SSE streaming for historical integrations, which helps with gradual rollback and hybrid paths during migration.<cite id="call_25d9fe551ab4-4">Claude’s French API docs describe streaming via SSE historically and outline handling server events for custom integrations</cite>

## Performance and operational trade-offs
Replacing SSE with Streamable HTTP simplifies the surface: one endpoint, request/response over POST, and SSE-only server streaming reduces protocol complexity and connection churn. Engineering analyses argue this addresses real-world pain points around long-lived SSE channels and multiple endpoints, improving scalability and reliability under load.<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">Anthropic’s move to Streamable HTTP is motivated by one endpoint and on-demand streaming to avoid SSE’s forced long connections</cite> However, SSE remains an option for high-throughput server-to-client paths; the spec notes servers can optionally leverage SSE to stream multiple messages, preserving low-latency characteristics while avoiding per-request long polls.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">Servers can optionally use SSE to stream multiple server messages in Streamable HTTP, enabling efficient multi-message delivery</cite>

Trade-offs to consider:
- Simplicity and ops: One endpoint and HTTP-native transport ease deployment, monitoring, and debugging compared to SSE’s one-way streaming model; backpressure is handled via HTTP streaming and application-layer controls rather than per-message polling overhead.<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">One endpoint and on-demand streaming simplify operations vs SSE’s persistent long connections</cite>
- Throughput/latency: SSE within Streamable HTTP preserves low-latency multi-message delivery; careful chunking and batching are still required to avoid small payload overheads and to respect client flow control.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">SSE can be used to stream multiple server messages efficiently from the Streamable HTTP endpoint</cite>
- Ecosystem maturity: Streamable HTTP is rapidly adopted in claude-code and third-party servers, but legacy SSE integrations may require temporary bridges or re-implementation to avoid feature gaps and bug regressions reported in issues.<cite id="call_ccd96c2d123d-0">claude-code supports Streamable HTTP, but migration issues highlight practical steps and current gaps</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-3">claude mcp add does not accept streamable-http as a transport type in some versions, despite documentation and third-party usage, indicating ecosystem maturity gaps</cite>

## Concrete implementation patterns
- Server setup (TypeScript SDK):
  - Choose McpServer with Streamable HTTP transport and define routes for /mcp (or your endpoint) handling JSON-RPC over POST and serving SSE via GET or chunked responses.
  - Use JSON-RPC notifications for server-to-client deltas (e.g., tool outputs, status updates) and requests over POST for client-bound commands; interleave SSE for high-throughput token streams when appropriate.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-2">The SDK recommends Streamable HTTP for remote servers and supports JSON-RPC over HTTP with SSE for streaming</cite><cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">Streamable HTTP uses HTTP POST for client-to-server and can optionally stream multiple server messages via SSE</cite>
- Client integration (Claude/claude-code):
  - Configure MCP servers with --transport streamable-http and point to the remote endpoint; Claude Code’s changelog confirms support for Streamable HTTP servers and community issues show usage for remote URLs (e.g., Smithery).<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-1">Claude Code v1.0.27 added support for Streamable HTTP MCP servers</cite><cite id="call_ccd96c2d123d-0">claude mcp add supports remote URLs for MCP servers using the new Streamable HTTP protocol</cite>
- Hybrid migration path:
  - Temporarily expose both SSE and Streamable HTTP endpoints during migration; gate client usage by feature flags or org settings, then retire SSE endpoints once clients and servers fully support Streamable HTTP. Claude’s MCP connector and SDKs ease this transition by abstracting transport selection and server discovery.<cite id="call_25d9fe551ab4-0">Claude’s MCP connector connects directly to remote MCP servers without a separate client, simplifying migration to new transports</cite><cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-1">The MCP changelog documents the move to Streamable HTTP and deprecation of HTTP+SSE</cite>

## Known issues and adoption status
Adoption is accelerating but not universal. Some tools still surface bugs where “claude mcp add” does not accept streamable-http as a transport, despite official docs and third-party integrations indicating support; this reflects packaging, versioning, and documentation lag in some distributions.<cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-3">claude mcp add does not accept streamable-http despite official docs and third-party MCP integrations referencing it</cite> Community issues also confirm that remote server support for Streamable HTTP is now available and widely used (e.g., Smithery), and that claude-code has merged a switch to the official MCP gem with Streamable HTTP transport in recent releases.<cite id="call_ccd96c2d123d-0">claude-code supports Streamable HTTP remote servers; issues confirm usage and current status</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-2">A pull request merged switching to the official MCP gem with Streamable HTTP transport in claude-code</cite> Anthropic’s MCP changelog explicitly calls out Streamable HTTP as the new primary transport and marks HTTP+SSE as legacy, reinforcing the migration direction for new integrations.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-1">The MCP changelog highlights Streamable HTTP as the new primary transport and deprecates HTTP+SSE</cite>

## How this compares to alternatives
- SSE (HTTP 1.1 Server-Sent Events): Historically used in MCP, SSE is simple for one-way streaming but ties updates to persistent open channels and can be less efficient for request/response round trips. Streamable HTTP replaces SSE with a single-purpose endpoint and uses POST for control and SSE only for streaming segments, improving operational scaling and request locality.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">Streamable HTTP uses HTTP POST for client-to-server and optional SSE for server-to-client multi-message streaming, decoupling control from streaming</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">Replacing SSE with Streamable HTTP avoids forced long connections and simplifies to one endpoint</cite>
- HTTP/2 Server Push: MCP’s Streamable HTTP does not mandate HTTP/2; it works over standard HTTP methods and content encodings, leveraging SSE where appropriate. This broadens compatibility with proxies and clients that may not support HTTP/2 push fully.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">The Streamable HTTP transport uses standard HTTP POST/GET and optional SSE, avoiding tight coupling to HTTP/2 push</cite>
- WebSockets: WebSockets are not the default MCP transport; Streamable HTTP keeps HTTP semantics for compatibility and ease of integration, while using SSE for streaming efficiency. WebSockets would complicate JSON-RPC routing and HTTP tooling; SSE + JSON-RPC blends better with existing HTTP stacks and tooling.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-4">MCP uses JSON-RPC over HTTP with optional SSE for streaming, preserving HTTP compatibility</cite>

## Practical guidance for adoption
- Prefer Streamable HTTP for new MCP servers and clients, especially in cloud-native deployments where HTTP proxies, load balancers, and SDKs are prevalent. It simplifies routing, authentication, and debugging while preserving low-latency streaming via SSE.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-2">Streamable HTTP is recommended for remote servers in the MCP SDK</cite><cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">SSE can be used to stream multiple server messages efficiently from a single Streamable HTTP endpoint</cite>
- For legacy SSE integrations, implement a compatibility layer that speaks both SSE and Streamable HTTP, or update clients to use Streamable HTTP first. Claude’s MCP connector and SDKs ease this transition by abstracting transport selection and server configuration.<cite id="call_25d9fe551ab4-0">Claude’s MCP connector connects directly to remote MCP servers without a separate client, reducing integration friction during transport upgrades</cite>
- Validate chunking and backpressure in production: tune server-side batch sizes and client-side read windows to balance throughput and latency; use HTTP/keep-alive and chunked transfer-encodings; implement graceful error recovery for SSE stream interruptions.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">The Streamable HTTP transport supports multiple client connections and optional SSE streaming of multiple messages, enabling chunked, controlled delivery</cite>

## Summary
Anthropic’s Streamable HTTP is a pragmatic evolution of MCP’s streaming model: a single HTTP endpoint, JSON-RPC over POST for control, and optional SSE for server-to-client streaming, designed to reduce operational complexity and improve scalability versus HTTP+SSE. It is now the recommended transport for remote MCP servers in official SDK guidance and is being adopted across Anthropic’s claude-code and third-party integrations, with migration tooling and configuration flags converging around --transport streamable-http. While SSE remains useful for high-throughput one-way updates within Streamable HTTP, the broader shift to Streamable HTTP addresses real-world pain points around persistent connections and endpoint proliferation, yielding simpler, more scalable streaming integrations.<cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-2">Streamable HTTP is recommended for remote servers in the MCP SDK</cite><cite id="call_f95de25e7e19-3">Streamable HTTP uses HTTP POST/GET and optional SSE to stream multiple messages from a single endpoint</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-0">Anthropic replaced HTTP+SSE with Streamable HTTP to simplify to one endpoint and avoid forced long connections</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-1">Claude Code added explicit support for Streamable HTTP MCP servers</cite><cite id="call_ccd96c2d123d-0">claude-code supports adding remote MCP servers via Streamable HTTP</cite><cite id="call_3f0a4013a089-3">Some clients still reject --transport streamable-http, reflecting ecosystem maturity gaps</cite>

Title: AI in Education: Where It Lands Today, What It Can Do, What Gets In the Way, and How to Build Systems That Sustain AI Top-Talent

Executive summary
Across learning, teaching, assessment, and administration, artificial intelligence in education (AIEd) is maturing from pilots to field deployments, with consistent evidence of small-to-moderate learning gains when interventions are well-integrated and evaluated in real classrooms.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">Reviews mapping the last decade of AIEd identify 13 roles of AI across learning, teaching, assessment, and administration, 7 learning outcomes, and 10 major challenges, underscoring both momentum and systemic barriers</cite>.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-0">Meta-analytic evidence from social experiments reports an overall small positive effect for intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) with medium effects on knowledge and small effects on skills, stronger for language domains and in primary/short-term deployments</cite>.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">A U.S. meta-analysis of 18 studies (77 effect sizes) finds a significant positive average effect (g≈0.27) with moderators including worked examples, duration, condition, learning outcome type, and immediate measurement</cite>.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies on ChatGPT shows improvements in academic performance, affective-motivational states, and higher-order thinking propensities, reductions in mental effort, and calls for stronger designs to test durability and validity</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Policy-oriented syntheses highlight privacy/ethical use, trustworthy algorithms, and equity/fairness as top trends and challenges, with recommendations for governance and research agendas</cite>.

1) Where AI is being deployed today: “落地场景” and what it changes
1.1 Personalized learning and tutoring at scale
- Intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) are embedded in classrooms and flipped-learning designs to adapt practice, feedback, and problem selection to learner knowledge states, often leveraging cognitive models or knowledge tracing.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">A decade-long review catalogs 13 AI roles including adaptive tutors and intelligent coaching within learning and teaching</cite>.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-0">Field studies of ITS show an overall g≈0.36 with medium effects on knowledge outcomes, stronger for language learning, and larger effects in primary grades and for interventions under one year</cite>.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">Across U.S. K–12, effects are significant overall and similar in elementary and middle schools, with lower effects in rural contexts and key moderators like worked examples and duration</cite>.
- Practical deployments include mastery learning platforms with stepwise problem streams, misconception diagnosis, and mastery-based progression; evidence suggests the largest gains when tutors align with curriculum pacing and provide immediate, worked-example-supported feedback.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">Worked examples and intervention duration emerge as key moderators of effect sizes</cite>.

1.2 Generative AI in classrooms and labs
- Generative AI (GenAI) assistants are being integrated into university courses and writing-intensive tasks, often as co-writers, editors, or tutors; early experimental evidence shows performance and affective benefits but warns about assessment validity and novelty effects.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">ChatGPT interventions predominantly occur at the university level across subjects, embedded in classroom practice, improving academic performance, affective-motivational states, higher-order thinking propensities, and reducing mental effort, with no significant effect on self-efficacy on average</cite>.
- Design patterns that strengthen “落地” include scaffolded prompts, code-walkthroughs, peer review with AI, and iterative drafting cycles; instructors report improved time-on-task and higher engagement when students learn to critique and steer AI outputs.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Propositions emphasize objective measures (e.g., originality, proctored assessments) and longer-term evaluations to separate novelty from durable gains</cite>.

1.3 Assessment, feedback, and learning analytics
- Automated grading and feedback loops for writing, programming, and math are used to increase formative frequency and reduce teacher workload; analytics dashboards surface at-risk patterns (engagement, concept mastery) and inform just-in-time interventions.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">AI roles span automated assessment and analytics within administration and teaching, with identified learning outcomes and challenges</cite>.
- Institutions deploy early-warning systems and adaptive remediation pathways; effectiveness varies with data quality, feature selection, and alignment to instructional goals.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The review highlights 10 major challenges that cut across learning, teaching, assessment, and administration</cite>.

1.4 Administrative and operational efficiency
- In administration, AI supports enrollment coordination, curriculum mapping, resource allocation, and plagiarism detection; adoption is driven by capacity to integrate structured data pipelines and guardrails for fairness and privacy.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">Roles in administration include workflow automation and decision support</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Policy experts identify privacy and trustworthy algorithms as central deployment challenges</cite>.

2) What gets in the way: practical challenges and risks
- Privacy, security, and ethics: Student data collection for analytics and model training raises consent, transparency, and security concerns; policy syntheses rank privacy/ethical use and trustworthy algorithms among the top challenges and priorities for governance.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Delphi research with international experts found privacy/ethical use, trustworthy algorithms, and equity/fairness as the three most impactful trends/challenges, with policy recommendations for trustworthy AI in education</cite>.
- Effectiveness and validity: Many studies are small, short-term, or post-test only; effect sizes for ITS and GenAI vary with design, domain, and measurement, and may attenuate over time or under routine use.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-0">Field effect sizes for ITS are small overall, with heterogeneity by domain and grade level</cite>.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Review calls for power analysis, proctored assessments, objective metrics, and long-term tracking to validate durable benefits</cite>.
- Equity and access: Benefits can be uneven across achievement levels, rural vs. urban contexts, and socioeconomic groups; interventions that rely on digital infrastructure and devices may exacerbate divides if not paired with support and inclusion strategies.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">Effects are lower in rural schools and vary by achievement level, with moderators indicating conditions matter</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Equity and fairness are repeatedly flagged as key deployment challenges</cite>.
- Teacher readiness and orchestration: Educators need training to integrate AI as a “human-AI partner,” design for critical thinking, and monitor for bias and overreliance; without scaffolding, adoption can devolve into “automation bias” or superficial use.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The review catalogs pedagogical challenges and suggests research directions to strengthen integration</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Trustworthy algorithms and human-in-the-loop design are central to effective deployment</cite>.
- Governance and accountability: Institutions struggle to define responsibility for AI-mediated decisions, ensure transparency in algorithmic assessments, and align with evolving regulatory requirements; policy guidance stresses clear ethics policies, auditability, and stakeholder engagement.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Policy recommendations include governance frameworks and research agendas to close gaps</cite>.

3) How education sustains AI top-talent: curricula, programs, and ecosystems
3.1 Curricular models and degree pathways
- Universities are building “AI + X” programs that embed machine learning, NLP, and systems thinking within domains like education, engineering, and economics; capstones and internships connect theory to AIEd problems (e.g., tutor design, assessment validity, learning analytics at scale).<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The AI roles across learning, teaching, assessment, and administration create a rich set of experiential project domains for students</cite>.
- Data-centric and ethics-infused curricula are rising: courses on responsible AI, privacy-preserving learning, and evaluation design are complementing core AI coursework to produce graduates who can build and govern AIEd systems.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Ethical use, trustworthy algorithms, and equity/fairness are emphasized as central competencies for graduates and institutional policy</cite>.

3.2 Research institutes and labs
- Dedicated AIEd labs and AI-for-education centers conduct learning science with AI, developing cognitive models, knowledge tracing, and analytics platforms validated in field settings; partnerships with K–12 and industry accelerate translational impact.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The review’s taxonomy supports targeted lab focus areas from adaptive learning to administrative decision support</cite>.
- In China, institutions have launched AI research institutes and AIEd initiatives aligned with national AI strategies, often integrating with local education bureaus for pilot deployments and teacher professional development.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">International policy syntheses note the need to embed ethics and equity in national strategies; Chinese initiatives typically mirror these priorities while emphasizing large-scale pilots</cite>.

3.3 Faculty development and industry linkages
- Faculty and instructional designers receive training in AI-mediated pedagogy, assessment design, and analytics literacy to act as “AI translators” between education and AI industries.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The identified challenges and opportunities motivate professional development to bridge research and practice</cite>.
- Industry partnerships supply real-world datasets, tools, and co-curricular experiences (e.g., hackathons, co-designed courses) that expose students to privacy-preserving AI, deployment constraints, and productization cycles.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Trustworthy AI and privacy-by-design are recurring themes in industry-facing curricula</cite>.

3.4 China-specific perspectives
- At the system level, China has prioritized AI talent cultivation through national strategies and “double-first-class” universities, with AIEd programs and AI+ disciplines expanding rapidly; pilots in smart classrooms and AI-assisted assessment are common, often co-led by MOE and tech firms.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Policy-oriented analyses emphasize aligning national strategies with ethical, trustworthy AI deployment; China’s initiatives reflect this pattern</cite>.
- In practice, universities leverage large language models for grading assistance, writing feedback, and coding tutoring, while piloting campus-wide learning analytics platforms to personalize advising and early-warning; these efforts are tempered by calls for governance, transparency, and validation.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Experimental evidence on GenAI in university courses supports targeted deployment with assessment safeguards</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Equity and privacy remain salient concerns for large-scale adoption</cite>.

4) How to strengthen the pipeline and ecosystem: evidence-based steps
4.1 Governance and policy scaffolds
- Adopt AIEd governance frameworks that mandate privacy-by-design, data minimization, consent transparency, and audit trails for algorithmic assessments and recommendations; integrate ethics and equity into accreditation and promotion criteria.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Policy recommendations emphasize privacy, trustworthy algorithms, and equity/fairness as governance priorities</cite>.
- Create cross-sector ethics review boards that include educators, students, and AI experts to evaluate AIEd deployments before scale; publish annual AIEd impact reports to build stakeholder trust.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Delphi-based policy guidance provides actionable recommendations for governance and oversight</cite>.

4.2 Pedagogy and orchestration
- Train instructors in “human-AI co-pedagogy”: prompt engineering for learning, critique of model outputs, and metacognitive scaffolds; prioritize tasks where AI complements human strengths (exploration, synthesis) and maintain high cognitive demand.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Evidence shows gains in higher-order thinking but stresses objective measures and design rigor</cite>.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">Worked examples and duration matter—design for sustained engagement</cite>.
- Use AI to personalize formative practice: combine ITS-style diagnostics with project-based assessments and proctored summative exams to preserve rigor while capturing durable learning gains.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-0">ITS effects are stronger for knowledge outcomes and in short, well-aligned interventions</cite>.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Propose complex, originality-aware assessments and proctoring to sustain validity</cite>.

4.3 Assessment and analytics
- Build learning analytics pipelines that integrate behavioral, performance, and socio-emotional indicators, then test interventions via randomized field experiments to determine effect sizes and equity impacts before district-wide rollout.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The review highlights analytics and early-warning as key AI roles with associated challenges</cite>.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">Meta-analytic moderators suggest design features that can amplify benefits</cite>.
- Ensure fairness: stratify analyses by subgroup (e.g., rural vs. urban, low-achieving), and iteratively adjust models and supports to reduce performance gaps; share open datasets and benchmarks with educators for community validation.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">Lower effects in rural schools and moderators by achievement level call for subgroup-aware design</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Equity and fairness are central challenges to address</cite>.

4.4 Talent development: curricula and experiential learning
- Integrate AIEd capstones/dissertations with real partners on projects like tutor evaluation, privacy-preserving knowledge tracing, or GenAI assessment assistants, requiring students to design studies, measure learning, and reflect on ethics and usability.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The catalog of AI roles provides authentic project domains for students</cite>.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Experimental evidence and methodological guidance inform rigorous project evaluation</cite>.
- Offer micro-credentials and short courses in responsible AI, learning analytics, and GenAI for educators to upskill quickly; embed “AI literacy” in general education to prepare future users and evaluators of AI systems.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Trustworthy AI and ethical use motivate modular professional development</cite>.

4.5 Industry and ecosystem partnerships
- Create industry-sponsored living labs where students and faculty co-design AIEd tools with K–12 partners, balancing innovation speed with privacy, safety, and evaluation requirements; fund fellowships for joint doctorates and postdocs focused on AIEd translation.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Policy analyses recommend aligning national strategies with trustworthy AI deployment and stakeholder engagement</cite>.
- Encourage open-source tooling for education (e.g., open knowledge-tracing, tutor platforms, privacy-preserving evaluation kits) to lower entry barriers and accelerate diffusion across institutions.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The review’s emphasis on challenges and opportunities motivates open, community-driven solutions</cite>.

5) Actionable roadmap for institutions and policymakers
- 90-day readiness checklist: inventory data flows and governance gaps; form an AIEd review board; pilot one high-impact use (e.g., ITS for language learning or GenAI writing support) with a randomized controlled design; plan subgroup monitoring and privacy safeguards.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-0">Field evidence suggests feasible, measurable gains with ITS when aligned to curriculum and domain</cite>.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">GenAI pilots should include objective, proctored assessments and power analysis</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Ethics and equity must be embedded from day one</cite>.
- 18–24 month scale-up plan: expand successful pilots to adjacent domains; launch educator micro-credentials and coaching; build analytics dashboards with fairness metrics; establish an annual AIEd impact and audit report with public release.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Policy guidance supports transparent governance and continuous improvement cycles</cite>.
- 3–5 year talent strategy: launch AIEd master’s and PhD tracks with industry co-advising; create national/continental networks for AIEd research and evaluation; fund large-scale RCTs to update effect-size estimates across contexts and languages.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-0">The systematic review identifies research gaps and future directions that can anchor degree-level learning outcomes</cite>.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">Meta-analytic moderators suggest targeted curricular and design levers to maximize impact</cite>.

6) Outlook
AIEd has moved beyond hype to a set of reproducible, field-proven patterns that can raise learning outcomes and engagement when embedded with human oversight, rigorous evaluation, and ethical guardrails.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-0">ITS field effects are small-to-moderate overall but substantial for knowledge outcomes, especially in language learning and primary settings</cite>.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Generative AI shows promise for performance and affective gains, provided assessments and designs address validity and durability</cite>.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Sustained success depends on privacy, fairness, and trustworthy AI governance, with education systems actively cultivating AI top-talent to drive the next wave of innovation</cite>.

Appendix: Key evidence highlights
- ITS in the field: g≈0.36 overall; medium effects on knowledge; stronger for language; larger in primary grades and short interventions.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-0">Field meta-analysis across 14 studies (N=3,496) reports g=0.36 with domain and grade-level heterogeneity</cite>.
- U.S. K–12 ITS: significant positive g≈0.27; similar in elementary and middle schools; lower in rural schools; worked examples and duration are key moderators.<cite id="call_5dec6b9b67eb-1">18 studies, 77 effect sizes show g=0.271 with moderators</cite>.
- GenAI in universities: experimental studies show improved performance, affect, higher-order thinking, reduced mental effort; recommendations include proctored assessments, objective metrics, and long-term tracking.<cite id="call_800e3dd3d434-0">Systematic review/meta-analysis across 69 articles (2022–2024) with design recommendations</cite>.
- Policy priorities: privacy/ethics, trustworthy algorithms, equity/fairness; governance frameworks and research agendas to guide deployment.<cite id="call_99ca2094067e-1">Delphi-based synthesis with international experts and actionable policy guidance</cite>.
</answer>

While cross-sectional studies have highlighted correlations between ChatGPT use and learning performance, they fall short of establishing causality. The findings reveal that ChatGPT interventions are predominantly implemented at the university level, cover various subject areas focusing on language education, are integrated into classroom environments as part of regular educational practices, and primarily involve direct student use of ChatGPT. This review presents four propositions from the findings: (1) distinguish between the quality of ChatGPT outputs and the positive effects of interventions on academic performance by shifting from well-defined problems in post-intervention assessments to more complex, project-based assessments that require skill demonstration, adopting proctored assessments, or incorporating metrics such as originality alongside quality; (2) evaluate long-term impacts to determine whether the positive effects on affective-motivational states are sustained or merely owing to novelty effect; (3) prioritise objective measures to complement subjective assessments of higher-order thinking; and (4) use power analysis to determine adequate sample sizes to avoid Type II errors and provide reliable effect size estimates. Especially with the advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and Wi-Fi-based sensing technologies offering promising solutions. These technologies can detect vital signs and human activity without physical contact, making them well suited to diverse healthcare environments. However, research on AI-enhanced Wi-Fi signal processing for health monitoring needs to be synthesized to understand its current capabilities, limitations, and potential. Objectives: This systematic review evaluates Channel State Information (CSI)-based Wi-Fi health monitoring systems, both with and without AI integration. It focuses on key advancements in vital signs detection, assessing the effectiveness of different AI techniques and identifying opportunities for future research. Methods: Following PRISMA and Kitchenham guidelines, we systematically searched six databases (IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, ACM Digital Library, Google Scholar, and ResearchGate-), retrieving 8,573 records. After screening, 45 published peer-reviewed studies from 2019 to 2024 were selected for analysis. The review focused on AI techniques, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Support Vector Machines (SVMs). Performance was evaluated using metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and sensitivity in scenarios, including multi-user detection and real-time applications. Results: Experimental findings revealed that AI models demonstrate high accuracy rates, achieving over 95% for heart rate and respiration monitoring, and demonstrate strong scalability and adaptability across various healthcare environments. However, significant challenges remain, including reduced performance in multi-person settings, privacy concerns, and computational efficiency limitations. Conclusions: AI-enhanced Wi-Fi sensing technologies show immense potential for non-invasive health monitoring, with high accuracy in vital sign detection. But challenges related to multi-user environments, privacy, and computational demands must be addressed. Future research should focus on overcoming these obstacles to advance AI-driven health monitoring technologies in clinical and home settings.</summary><hostname>PeerJ</hostname><author_list><author name="Murad Al-Rajab" affiliation="Abu Dhabi University, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates" /><author name="Kamel Qassem" affiliation="Abu Dhabi University, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates" /><author name="Sara Seyam" affiliation="Abu Dhabi University, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates" /><author name="Youssef Al Hamadi" affiliation="Cleveland Clinic Hospital, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates" /><author name="Ahmed Hadi Al-Dubaisi" affiliation="Cleveland Clinic Hospital, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates" /><author name="Jihad Mallat" affiliation="Bradford Institution for Health Research, Bradford, United Kingdom" /><author name="Joan Lu" affiliation="Leeds Beckett University, Leeds, United Kingdom" /><author name="Samer H. raw_output.raw_text: <search query="thermal vision respiration heartbeat phase demodulation deep learning accuracy non-contact 2022..2025" search_time="2026年5月12日17时7分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:19"><title>Non-Contact Respiration Rate Measurement From Thermal Images Using Multi-Resolution Window and Phase-Sensitive Processing</title><summary>This paper presents a method for measuring human respiration using a thermal camera. Respiration, being a commonly monitored biomedical signal, has traditionally been measured using contact-based methods, which can cause discomfort and skin damage to patients. With the need for non-contact respiration measurement to prevent infection in the post-COVID-19 era, previous studies encountered challenges in applying non-contact methods in clinical settings due to the distortion of respiratory signals caused by high-dimensional filters. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the use of a thermal camera for non-contact data acquisition and accurate respiratory rate (RR) prediction, even in the presence of noisy respiratory signals. The proposed method leverages a multi-resolution window (MW) and phase-sensitive (PS) processing. Specifically, thermal images are captured using an infrared (IR) thermal camera, and the respiratory signal is extracted from the series of thermal images. The MW method, employing three windows of different sizes in the time domain, is then applied to the extracted respiratory signal. The resulting MW output is transformed into the frequency domain using the Fourier synchro-squeezed transform (FSST). The PS processing involves the multiplication of the converted signal, which is in polar form after a phasor operation. The processed data is utilized to train two bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (bi-LSTM) networks, and the RR is calculated based on the trained model. To validate the proposed model, a total of 37 surgical patients were involved, with 20 patients used for training and 17 patients for testing. Six deep learning models were designed and their performances were compared. The results indicate that the proposed model outperformed the others, achieving a test classification accuracy of 98.06% and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.381. Despite being non-invasive and non-contact, our method demonstrates high accuracy in predicting RR, attributed to the utilization of MW and PS processing. Therefore, it holds potential for application in clinical environments, such as monitoring patients with pulmonary diseases or in intensive care units (ICUs).</summary><hostname>YUHSpace</hostname><publisher>IEEE Access</publisher><author_list><author name="Jiwon Choi" affiliation="1 Department of Medical Engineering, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea; 2 Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea" /><author name="Kyeongtaek Oh" affiliation="1 Department of Medical Engineering, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea; 2 Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea" /><author name="Oyun Kwon" affiliation="1 Department of Medical Engineering, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea; 2 Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea" /><author name="Jun Hwan Kwon" affiliation="1 Department of Medical Engineering, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea; 2 Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea" /><author name="Jeongmin Kim" affiliation="1 Department of Medical Engineering, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea; 2 Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul 03722, Republic of Korea" /><author name="And Sun K Yoo" affiliation="1 Department of Medical Engineering, Yonsei Unive

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="mmWave FMCW vital signs respiration heart rate deep learning transformer accuracy 2022..2025" search_time="2026年5月12日17时10分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:19"><title>Multi-Feature Transformer-Based Learning for Remote and Accurate Vital Sign Estimation Using mmWave FMCW Radar</title><summary>Non-contact measurement of vital signs is an important issue in modern healthcare, aimed at enhancing patient comfort and convenience. Achieving sufficient measurement distance and adaptability to patient movement is essential for effectiveness. Current research covers measurement ranges between 1 and 3.5 meters. This study introduces a novel multifeature transformer-based super-resolution model. By inputting and encoding low-resolution sequences of distance, phase, and phase variation rates, the model upsamples these sequences, generating additional sample points and transforming the lowresolution data into high-resolution sequences. This process improves the quality and range of FMCW radar measurements by increasing the sample points, enabling the model to extract vital sign information from low-resolution sequences and produce accurate results. From the generated high-resolution sequences, vital signs such as heart rate and respiration are then extracted. Experimental results show that, at a distance of 5 meters, the system achieves 87.3 accuracy for heart rate and 89.1 accuracy for respiration in a walking scenario, outperforming existing solutions by 8.6 % and 6.5 %, respectively.</summary><hostname>IEEE Xplore</hostname><cite_count>1</cite_count><author_list><author name="Yuh-Shyan Chen" /><author name="Jhuo-Han Lyu" /><author name="Chih-Shun Hsu" /></author_list><url>https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10978740</url><publish_time>2025年3月24日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:20"><title>Convolutional Neural Networks for the Real-Time Monitoring of Vital Signs Based on Impulse Radio Ultrawide-Band Radar during Sleep</title><summary>Vital signs provide important biometric information for managing health and disease, and it is important to monitor them for a long time in a daily home environment. To this end, we developed and evaluated a deep learning framework that estimates the respiration rate (RR) and heart rate (HR) in real time from long-term data measured during sleep using a contactless impulse radio ultrawide-band (IR-UWB) radar. The clutter is removed from the measured radar signal, and the position of the subject is detected using the standard deviation of each radar signal channel. The 1D signal of the selected UWB channel index and the 2D signal applied with the continuous wavelet transform are entered as inputs into the convolutional neural-network-based model that then estimates RR and HR. From 30 recordings measured during night-time sleep, 10 were used for training, 5 for validation, and 15 for testing. The average mean absolute errors for RR and HR were 2.67 and 4.78, respectively. The performance of the proposed model was confirmed for long-term data, including static and dynamic conditions, and it is expected to be used for health management through vital-sign monitoring in the home environment.</summary><hostname>MDPI</hostname><publisher>Sensors 2023, 23, 3116</publisher><author_list><author name="Sang Ho Choi" affiliation="School of Computer and Information Engineering, Kwangwoon University, Seoul 01897, Republic of Korea" /><author name="Heenam Yoon" affiliation="Department of Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, Sangmyung University, Seoul 03016, Republic of Korea" /></author_list><url>https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/23/6/3116/pdf?version=1678806077</url><publish_time>2023年3月14日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:21"><title>mm-Wave Radar-Based Vital Signs Monitoring and Arrhythmia Detection Using Machine Learning</title><summary>A non-contact, non-invasive monitoring system to measure and estimate the heart and breathing rate of humans using a frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) mm-wave radar at 77 GHz

1) 摘要
中国的艺术生长期集中于传统艺术机构、教育系统与文创企业，但数字化与平台经济正在消解行业边界，催生“跨界多元发展”形态。研究与实践表明，通过“新文科/新艺科”课程重构、行业–教育融合、项目制与成果转化机制，艺术生可向创意科技、品牌体验、文化IP等复合型岗位跃迁；然而，就业形态升级常滞后于就业质量提升，需政府、高校与企业共建支持体系。社会评价体系若过度依赖竞赛与专业审美筛选，易扭曲资源分配、压缩普通学生的参与空间；强化知识产权交易与文化消费升级，有助于提升创作收益与职业尊严。国际上，北欧的制度性保障、欧盟的结构性基金与市场孵化机制、美国的平台化与资本介入、日韩的产业政策与版权强保护，提供了可资借鉴的路径。关键挑战在于如何将评价改革、产权激励与市场需求有效耦合，以实现艺术人才的社会流动与收入改善。

2) 背景与趋势：艺术生就业边界的消融
艺术与科技、商业、教育等领域的边界正在加速模糊。有研究指出，艺术类毕业生的就业形态已从“固守单一专业领域”向“探索跨界多元发展”转变，但就业质量提升未能同步，亟需构建政府、高校、企业协同的社会支持体系来拓展与优化就业路径<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">在文化产业与数字经济深度融合的背景下，艺术类毕业生就业形态呈现跨界多元发展的新态势，但就业质量提升滞后，需政府、高校、企业协同构建社会支持体系以拓展与优化就业路径</cite>。行业–教育脱节与技能–需求错配长期存在，艺术生面临专业技能与市场需求不匹配、职业路径不清晰、岗位供给有限与竞争激烈并存的困境<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-2">艺术生面临专业技能与市场需求不匹配、职业发展路径不明确、就业岗位有限与竞争压力大等困境</cite>。部分高校正尝试以“慢就业”为锚点，通过个性化服务与职业规划提升匹配度，缓解结构性矛盾<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-1">针对艺术类高校毕业生慢就业现象，提出完善就业服务体系、改良学校教育与家庭观念更新，通过转变态度、创新方法、提升匹配度与个性化服务推动顺利就业</cite>。

技术融合重塑艺术生产范式。数字化新媒体环境下，艺术设计人才培养从传统媒体视觉设计向新媒体视觉设计转型，课程与定位亟待重构<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-0">数字化新媒体环境下，艺术设计类人才需求从传统媒体视觉设计转向新媒体视觉设计，推动人才培养定位、方向与课程设置重构</cite>。新一代信息技术（5G、云计算、大数据、物联网、AI、区块链）与文创产业的深度融合，正在突破传统艺术概念，生成跨学科新方向；研究者正探索如何引入大数据思维、弥合技术基础短板、培育“艺技商创”型创新人才<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">5G、云、大数据、IoT、AI与区块链与文创产业的深融推动艺术突破传统概念并生成新学科方向；研究聚焦于艺术生如何引入大数据、补足技术基础与培养艺技商创融合的创新人才</cite>。产业端的升级倒逼教育改革，家用纺织品设计专业以“艺技商创”理念对接家纺产业价值链高端，通过STEAM式融合解决“重艺轻技、缺商弱创”问题，形成可迁移的跨界能力模型<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-2">针对家纺产业价值链高端化，提出“创意融合技术、创新提升价值”理念，以艺技商创融合模式解决重艺轻技、缺商弱创问题</cite>。

3) 破界路径：能力升级与教育模式创新
能力升级的四个维度。面向融合型岗位，能力模型需从单一技艺向“艺术感知×技术素养×商业思维×项目能力”跃迁。教学改革上，数字化媒体艺术专业正构建“艺术与产业交叉发展”的教学系统，推动真实项目驱动、跨学科协同，以适配技术革命与产业转型的需求<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-3">提出数字媒体艺术专业应构建与产业交叉发展的教学系统，推进教学改革与实践教学，以适应技术革命与产业转型</cite>。在“新文科/新艺科”框架下，研究聚焦于如何将大数据等技术方法引入艺术学习、诊断技术基础缺口，并设计更易理解的融合范式，从而孵化出可落地的“艺技商创”能力<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">研究探索在艺术教育中引入大数据技术、选择可理解的融合模型、补足技术基础，以培养艺技商创融合的创新人才</cite>。

教育模式的三大转向。第一，重构课程体系与能力图谱。以产业需求为锚，打破专业壁垒，将编程、数据分析、交互设计、用户研究等模块嵌入艺术类课程，形成“技术素养+艺术表达+商业洞察”能力链<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-0">数字化新媒体环境下，人才培养定位、方向与课程设置需重构，以适配新媒体视觉设计需求</cite><cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-2">艺技商创融合模式强调创意与技术、商业与创新并重，以应对产业价值链高端化</cite>。第二，推行项目制与成果转化。通过项目制课程与教学成果转化体系，将创意转化为产品、服务与市场价值，提升就业竞争力与创业能力<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-3">构建项目导向的教学系统，强化实践教学与跨学科整合，以适配产业变革</cite>。第三，深化产教融合与就业服务。行业–教育融合的就业模式强调真实项目、联合培养与订单式服务，以提升毕业生的岗位适配度与职业发展清晰度<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-3">就业模式改革需对接产业变革，构建跨行业发展的教学系统与实践路径</cite><cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-1">完善就业服务体系、创新个性化服务与学校教育改良有助于提升匹配度与就业质量</cite>。

4) 就业生态：平台、项目与跨界机会
平台化就业生态正在形成。数字化平台与新媒体业态为艺术生提供内容创作、交互设计、视觉传达等入口职位，使个人作品可直接触达用户与市场，降低传统中介依赖。研究显示，艺术生需在“守界”与“跨界”间找到平衡，政府、高校与企业应共同搭建资源对接、创业孵化与权益保障的平台，以支撑就业形态升级后的质量跃迁<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">就业形态从守界到跨界转变过程中，需政府、高校、企业协同构建社会支持体系，以拓展与优化就业路径与质量</cite>。在平台与项目驱动下，新兴岗位群包括：文创IP策划与运营、品牌体验与视觉叙事、数字内容生产与用户增长、交互与空间设计、文化数据分析等，这些岗位对“艺术表达+商业逻辑+技术工具”复合能力提出刚性需求<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">技术与文创产业融合催生新学科方向与岗位，艺术生需补足技术基础并掌握可落地的融合模式</cite><cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-2">艺技商创理念指向创意与技术、商业与创新并重的能力结构，适配新兴岗位群</cite>。

5) 社会评价体系：审美筛选、竞赛导向与市场扭曲
当前评价体系的双重困境。其一，专业审美与竞赛导向挤压多元价值。在应试与“官本位”惯性下，中小学与基层文艺活动常以专业评委、层层选拔与奖状为指挥棒，导致资源向少数特长生集中、普通学生被边缘化、审美标准“专业化”与“表演化”，并造成有限教育资金外流与低效投入<cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-0">艺术教育需尊重艺术规律与多元取向并建立教学质量评价体系，避免简单化与单一化</cite><cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-2">文艺调演类活动的组织与审美评价过度专业化，导致少数特长生受益、多数学生被忽视，并造成教育资源浪费与资金外流</cite>。其二，高等教育评价仍存质量与结构失衡。扩招背景下，艺术类院校面临师资不足、教学质量下降与就业压力上升，研究呼吁重建以艺术规律与多元发展为导向的教学质量评价体系，而非唯竞赛、唯奖状论<cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-0">扩招导致生均资源紧张、师资不足与教学质量下降，艺术教育需建立尊重艺术规律与多元发展的教学质量评价体系</cite>。

评价体系对发展与收入的影响。过度强调专业审美筛选与竞赛获奖，会引导学生与市场将精力集中于“可展演、可获奖”的小众技艺，弱化用户需求洞察、商业转化与平台运营能力；这不仅限制就业面，也压缩收入提升空间。研究显示，艺术生普遍面临技能–需求错配与岗位供给有限的困境，而评价体系未能有效激励面向市场的多元能力，从而抑制收入增长与职业流动性<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-2">艺术生面临技能与市场需求不匹配、职业路径不明确与竞争激烈等困境</cite><cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-2">审美评价专业化与竞赛导向导致资源错配与学生负担，与素质教育与创新人才培养目标相悖</cite>。

改革方向。建立多元评价矩阵：将用户价值、商业逻辑、技术工具使用、项目成果与社会影响纳入评价维度；推广基于真实项目的“过程性评价”与“成果交易性评价”；鼓励跨学科作品集（Portfolio）评审，并引入产业导师与用户反馈；在基础教育阶段减少“展演锦标赛”权重，增加全员参与的审美体验与创造力培养<cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-0">应建立尊重艺术规律与多元发展的教学质量评价体系，而非单一化评价</cite><cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">在艺术教育中引入大数据等技术方法，并补足技术基础，有助于提升面向市场的多元能力</cite>。

6) 知识产权保护与文化消费升级：对艺术人才经济待遇的影响
IP保护与交易机制的经济效应。在平台化与数字化背景下，版权确权、交易与授权运营成为艺术人才变现的关键路径。研究认为，艺术与科技融合将催生大量可版权化的内容与体验，而艺术生需掌握基础的技术工具与数据思维，才能将创意转化为可交易的IP资产；同时，政策与市场对文化IP的重视将提升创作收益与职业尊严<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">技术与文创产业融合催生新学科方向与可交易的内容形态，艺术生需补足技术基础并掌握融合范式以实现价值转化</cite>。然而，当前艺术生普遍缺乏清晰的IP运营知识与渠道资源，导致作品难以进入市场循环；教育系统也缺乏系统的版权知识与交易实训模块，制约了经济收益的释放<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-2">艺术生面临职业路径不明确与技能–需求错配，反映出教育体系与市场需求脱节，影响就业与收入</cite>。

文化消费升级的拉力。随着消费者对个性化、体验化与高品质文化产品的需求上升，文创与沉浸式体验等领域的岗位需求与支付意愿提高，艺术人才可通过品牌合作、定制化服务与会员制运营获得更高议价能力。但市场教育仍有短板：多数艺术生缺乏用户研究、数据分析与商业模型训练，难以匹配消费升级背后的运营能力要求；因此，版权保护与文化消费的升级需与教育改革、孵化平台共同作用，才能有效转化为收入提升<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-0">数字化新媒体环境下，人才需求转向新媒体视觉设计，推动课程与能力升级</cite><cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-2">艺技商创融合模式强调商业思维与创新能力，适配消费升级催生的岗位需求</cite>。

政策与制度的作用。强化IPT保护、降低交易成本与完善授权中介，有助于提升艺术人才的版权收益；同时，文化消费升级依赖于市场教育与基础设施（如内容平台、数据工具与金融工具）。研究建议将IPT知识、授权谈判、平台运营纳入艺术类课程，并通过孵化器与经纪机构连接市场，从而打通“创作–确权–交易–反馈”闭环，提升经济待遇与职业稳定性<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">在艺术教育中引入技术方法与版权意识，有助于提升作品的可交易性与市场价值</cite><cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">需社会支持体系支撑跨界就业质量提升，包括市场连接与权益保障</cite>。

7) 国际经验与可借鉴模式
北欧：制度性保障与社会安全网。北欧国家通过高税收、高福利与全民艺术教育，保障艺术家基本生活，使艺术成为公共服务体系的一部分；文化机构与社会企业合作孵化项目，降低个体风险，鼓励跨界实验。这种制度设计提升了艺术的社会地位，并为人才流动提供安全保障。中国可借鉴其社会保障托底与公共文化投入的思路，降低艺术跨界试错成本<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">需政府、高校、企业协同构建社会支持体系，以拓展与优化艺术类毕业生的就业路径与质量</cite>。

欧盟：结构性基金与平台孵化网络。欧盟通过“创意欧洲”等计划，为艺术与科技融合项目提供定向资助与跨国孵化资源，并建立版权交易平台与中介服务体系，促进作品跨境流通与收益提升。中国可借鉴其项目制资助与平台化中介经验，完善国内版权交易与孵化网络<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">技术与文创产业融合催生新学科方向与可交易内容形态，需制度与平台支持以实现价值转化</cite>。

美国：市场驱动与资本介入。美国艺术院校深度嵌入硅谷与时尚产业，强调用户增长、数据驱动与商业模型训练；艺术生在游戏、影视、广告与消费品牌中承担关键角色，收入与社会地位随市场成功显著上升。中国可借鉴其“用户思维、数据素养、商业闭环”三位一体的能力培养模式，并警惕过度市场化导致的资源马太效应<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-2">艺技商创融合模式强调创意、技术与商业并重，适配市场驱动的岗位需求</cite>。

日韩：产业政策与版权强保护。日本与韩国通过产业政策引导艺术与科技融合（如动漫、游戏、智能设计），并以严格的版权法与集体管理组织保障创作者收益；高校与产业界共建实验室与联合公司，实现人才培养与创收并举。中国可借鉴其“政策引导+法律保障+产教实体”模式，提升艺术人才的经济待遇与职业尊严<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">技术与文创产业融合推动新方向与商业模式，需法律与组织保障以实现可持续收益</cite>。

本土可迁移经验。中国部分职业院校与产业共建“艺技商创”模式，已验证可行：通过课程嵌入技术工具、项目制对接产业需求、成果导向的评价体系，显著提升学生的就业广度与创业能力；建议在本科院校推广“微专业”“交叉工作坊”与“驻场导师制”，并配套创业基金与版权服务站，形成可复制的升级路径<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-2">艺技商创融合模式在职业教育中的成功实践为本科改革提供可迁移经验</cite><cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-3">构建与产业交叉的教学系统与项目导向的实践路径，有助于提升就业竞争力</cite>。

8) 行动清单：面向艺术生的多元化发展指南
个人层：能力矩阵与作品集策略
- 构建“艺技商创”能力链：至少掌握一项艺术表达专长+一项技术工具（如编程、数据分析、交互设计）+一项商业分析框架（用户画像、价值主张、ROI意识）<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">引入大数据等技术方法与补足技术基础，有助于艺术生掌握可落地的融合能力</cite><cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-2">艺技商创融合强调创意、技术与商业并重，适配多元岗位</cite>。
- 作品集（Portfolio）转型：从“技艺秀”转向“问题陈述+用户证据+技术实现+商业模型”四元结构，并嵌入可授权或可交易模块（如数字藏品、体验原型）<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">技术与文创融合催生可交易的内容形态，需补足技术基础与可落地的模式</cite>。
- 职业锚点选择：瞄准文创IP、品牌体验、数字内容、空间交互、文化数据等岗位，准备对应的项目经验与成果证据<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-0">数字化新媒体环境下，人才需求从传统媒体向新媒体视觉设计转型，推动课程与能力升级</cite>。

教育层：课程、项目与评价升级
- 课程微认证：在院校内争取“数字素养”“数据分析”“交互设计”“IP运营”等微证书学分，或通过MOOC与企业共建课程<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">在艺术教育中引入大数据等技术方法，补足技术基础</cite>。
- 项目制与成果转化：加入跨学科项目组，争取真实客户项目与孵化资源，通过“项目制课程→中试孵化→市场交易”闭环积累作品集与收入证据<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-3">构建项目导向的教学系统与实践路径，提升就业竞争力</cite>。
- 评价改革：推动加入用户反馈、交易指标（如授权意向、用户量、留存率）与社会影响的多元评价，提升市场适配性<cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-0">建立尊重艺术规律与多元发展的教学质量评价体系</cite>。

机构层：平台、基金与中介建设
- 学校：设立“跨界创新中心”或“艺科实验室”，引入驻场设计师、工程师与投资人；开设IP运营与版权交易实训模块<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">需政府、高校、企业协同构建社会支持体系，支撑跨界就业质量提升</cite><cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">技术与文创融合催生新方向，需制度与平台支持</cite>。
- 区域：搭建“版权登记—交易撮合—法律咨询—税务结算”一站式服务站，降低交易成本与风险；组织跨界工作坊与沙盘模拟，提升实战能力<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">补足技术基础与可落地的融合模式有助于提升交易可能性</cite>。
- 个人：加入自由职业者协会与版权联盟，获取合同模板、维权指导与市场情报，建立个人品牌与客户池<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">社会支持体系包括权益保障与市场连接</cite>。

9) 局限与未来数据需求
现有研究多为定性分析与院校个案，缺乏全国范围内的：（1）艺术生就业质量与收入的长面板数据，按专业、性别、生源地分层；（2）IPT保护强度与艺术人才收入、授权频次的定量关联；（3）文化消费升级指数与艺术岗位薪资、创业成功率的结构化证据；（4）国际比较中艺术家社会地位（如基本收入保障、文化岗位占比、税收补贴）的权威统计。建议由教育部与统计局牵头，联合文化部与知识产权局，开展“艺术人才发展追踪调查”并发布年度白皮书；同时引入世界银行/UNESCO的国际比较框架，建立可跨期比对的指标体系。这将为政策设计与资源配置提供更精确的依据<cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">就业质量提升滞后于形态变化，需系统性政策支持</cite><cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-0">需建立尊重规律与多元发展的评价体系，以引导资源有效配置</cite>。

结语
突破传统就业领域的枷锁，关键在于重构能力、重塑评价、重建生态。当艺术生掌握技术工具与商业思维、作品集承载用户价值与版权资产、院校与平台共同降低跨界成本时，多元化职业路径与更优厚的经济待遇将成为常态。而这一转型的成败，取决于社会评价体系能否从“技艺竞赛”转向“价值创造”，以及知识产权保护与文化消费升级能否形成正向循环，最终提升艺术人才的社会地位与经济尊严<cite id="call_f5e0d96ac29f-1">技术与文创融合推动新方向与商业模式，艺术生需补足技术基础与可落地的融合能力</cite><cite id="call_a0ee41d32189-0">需政府、高校、企业协同构建社会支持体系，支撑跨界就业质量提升</cite><cite id="call_b7aebd98111a-2">审美评价专业化与竞赛导向导致资源错配，需改革评价体系以激发创新</cite>。
</answer>

reference_id="<|superscript|>:2"><title>关于中小学文艺调演形式的改革建议</title><summary>多少年来，中小学每年的文艺调演其组织形式是逐级会演，层层筛选，类似体育上的淘汰赛，基层学校的节目参加区、县级选拔；选上的优秀节目参加市级会演；若遇到省级、国家级调演再逐级推选优秀节目参赛。教育行政部门的这种文艺活动组织形式和应试教育中宝塔似的人才培养机制一脉相承。其弊端显而易见。一、文艺调演成了名利场，客观上误导艺术教育的发展方向随着教育改革的不断深入，1987年4月国务院制定《中华人民共和国国民经济和社会发展第七个五年计划（1986—1990）》中规定：“各级各类学校都要加强思想政治工作，贯彻德育、智育、体育、美育全面发展的方针，把学生培养成为有理想、有文化、有纪律的社会主义建设人才”。1994年第二次全国教育工作会议在北京召开，美育成为会议一项重要议题。李岚清副总理指出：“学校的美育对于培养全面发展人才具有重要作用，应该切实加强。”第三次全国教育工作会议为切实提高美育在学校教育中的地位采取了重大举措。将美育的实施途径“不仅从课堂教学延伸到课外全面，把美育融进学校教育全过程，而且从学校拓展到社会美育大环境，美育的内涵由此得到了极大的丰富。”（郭声健《从三次全国教育工作会议看美育地位的稳步提高》）随着美育地位的提高，人们开始注重艺术教育。国家组织专人对各省艺术教育工作进行检查，此举本是促进艺术教育发展，根本目的是深化教育改革，全面推进素质教育，培养21世纪民族振兴所需的创新人才。但上面的意图、政策往往到了下面贯彻时就走样了。基层为了迎接检查，展示素质教育成果，格外看重各级文艺调演的奖状，为获得奖状，不惜重金请专业团体名人编排节目，挑选出文艺特长生，加班加点排练。服装、道具、化妆，一切向专业团体看齐。比赛完，拿到奖的如获至宝，眉开眼笑；未获奖的则垂头丧气。此种组织形式使得基层学校劳民伤财，叫苦不迭。与国家加强艺术教育工作，深化教育改革，全面推进素质教育，培养社会所需创新人才的根本宗旨相违背，客观上误导了学校艺术教育的发展方向。二、文艺调演成为少数特长生的专利，与广大中小学生无关为了迎接文艺调演，取得好成绩，各校均选出文艺特长生，加班加点排练，这可苦了有文艺特长的学生，为了给学校增光，丧失了自己自由自在的课余生活，打乱了学习秩序。而这一切则与学校绝大多数学生无关。“事不关己，高高挂起”，绝大多数学生对此事漠不关心，有的甚至根本不知道。拿出的高质量节目给谁看呢？是给少数专家评委看的，广大青少年学生根本看不到。我市今年文化局、教委联合举办的“六—专场为例，凭票人场，而票呢？则发给了机关各级领导，结果是“六—专场观众多是成人，孩子们看不到自己的节目。美国音乐教育家本耐特·雷默所撰《21世纪音乐教育面临的挑战》中谈到学生如何创造正在聆听的音乐。它加强了音乐体验的另一尺度——音乐创造想像力的尺度。音乐想像力也必须在听觉中出现，因为听觉是一种创造性行为。如果少数特长生付出艰辛艺术劳动，精排的节目能让广大青少年学生欣赏，这也值得。这也是艺术教育面向全体学生的一种形式。可事实情况并非如此，往往精排的节目只有领导和评委能看到。这种延袭多年的文艺调演组织形式，既是应试教育体制下的产物，也显现出中国社会文化“官本位”意识浓厚的一面，有关的组织者、操作者，其心态是创造轰动效应，拿出“政绩”给上级领导看，而未真正考虑广大青少年的审美需求，没考虑到做为一种健康的校园文化，应得到广大青少年的承认和欢迎。三、有限的教育资金外流，造成不必要的浪费中共中央党校副校长王伟光在《新时期人民内部矛盾的新情况、新问题、新特点及解决对策》一文中谈到“我国是在国民经济高速运行中推进经济体制改革的，在新旧体制转换过程中还要保持经济的高速增长，因此整个经济环境相对紧张。”2000年参加中小学音乐国家级骨干教师培训的第一批学员中，来自安排单师培训的一位小学教师就接连几个月未领工资，教育部发的每月450元生活补贴，他省下来买业务资料，自己天天吃方便面。可每年地方上中小学文艺调演，却花去大量资金。我市一所小学，请歌舞团的国家一级编导编一个舞，要价是1500元。这在我们低收人、低消费的城市，价格已不菲了。可各学校对此经费使用从不吝啬，因为按以往经验，节目要想获奖，就非得请专业的名家指点，不花钱，学校师生自己创编的节目是肯定通不过专家评审，被淘汰的。这样，众多单位都去请专家，可想而知，原本短缺的教育资金，却挤出一部分，流人了少数专家的口袋。不仅如此，为了使评审具权威性，各级举办单位，不惜花钱请专业团体的名家来当评委。年年如此，有谁来细算这笔帐，这些钱省下来能使多少过学生重返校园。今年我市妇联开展救助失学女童的“春蕾”活动，仅从怀远县徐圩乡摸排出的失学女童名单就厚厚一本，向社会呼吁捐助500元钱，就可供一个孩子读完小学，可直到“六—节”，厚厚名单中只有5个孩子获得了赞助，一边是失学女童问题无力解决，这难道不该引起教育部门行政官员的深思吗？四、审美评价上“专业化”倾向严重，不利于创新人才培养中小学的文艺调演，就其性质而言，是业余的校园文化生活，永远不会成为专业文艺。第三次全国教育工作会议上，李鹏总理指出，中小学美育“重点还是着力于陶冶情操，提高道德修养”。第三次全国教育工作会议上部署式上，江总书记就我国的教育方针做了新的表述“我们必须全面贯彻党的教育方针，坚持教育为社会主义、为人民服务，坚持教育与社会实践相结合，以提高国民素质为根本宗旨，以培养学生的创新精神和实践能力为重点，努力造就‘有理想、有道德、有文化、有纪律’的德育、智育、体育、美育全面发展的社会主义事业的建设者和接班人”。但目前的这种中小学文艺调演组织形式，请文艺界的专家权威来评审节目，其审美评价标准不符合素质教育注重人的创新精神、创新能力的培养目标，“专业化”倾向非常严重，学生的舞蹈，一招一式要符合专业训练
